sentences.text: Captioned petition is filed by the land owner feeling aggrieved by the letter addressed by respondent No.2- Tahsildar as per Annexure-B wherein respondent No.2- Tahsildar has called upon the petitioner-land owners to offer their explanation within 24 hours.
Challenging the same, the captioned petition is filed.
2. The petitioner claims to be the owner of land bearing Survey No.69/1 measuring 2 acre 4 guntas.
Petitioner's grievance is that respondent No.2 intends to erect high power tension tower and transmission line in the lands owned by the petitioner.

Petitioner claims that the present petition land is lifeline and it is only the source of livelihood and therefore, petitioner is requesting the respondents to acquire the land and pay compensation under the provisions of Land Acquisition Act.
Feeling aggrieved by the impugned communication sent by respondent No.2, the captioned petition is filed and this court has granted interim order.
4. The respondents have filed statement of objections and have also sought for vacating the interim order granted by this Court.

Respondent No.3 claims that there is prior approval from the competent authority under Section 68 of the Electricity Act, 2003, and pursuant to application submitted by respondent No.3 for grant of licence, the authority has granted licence.
The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission has granted licence to respondent No.3 and therefore respondent No.3 is conferred with powers under Section 164 of the Electricity Act, 2003.

Therefore,
respondent No.3 claims that it has power to lay telegraph lines and therefore, the petitioner though owner of the land in question has no locus to obstruct respondent No.3 from laying overhead lines.
5. Heard the counsel for the petitioner and the learned HCGP appearing for respondents 1 and 2 and the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.3.

I have NC: 2023:KHC-D:10478 examined the Sumasrinivas Desai vs The Deputy Commissioner on 12 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128472869/
2 claim made by the petitioner and the stand taken by respondent No.3 in the statement of objections.

sentences.text: On examining the statement of objections, it is clearly born out from the records that respondent No.3 having assumed status of telegraph authority is entitled to lay lines.
The petitioner, who is lawful owner, is equally entitled to receive compensation.

The material on record clearly indicates that there is obstruction of the land in question and therefore, respondent No.3 though assumes status of telegraph authority has to seek appropriate orders at the hands of the District Magistrate by having recourse to Section 16 of the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885.
The petitioner/land owner is equally entitled to seek appropriate compensation under Section 10-D of the Act.
If there is obstruction, respondent No.3 has to seek permission under section 16(1) of the Indian Telegraph Act.
Reserving liberty to respondent No.3 to seek appropriate permission from the District Magistrate under Section 16(1) of the Act, the writ petition needs to be allowed.

The impugned endorsement issued by respondent No.2-Tahasildar is one without NC: 2023:KHC-D:10478 jurisdiction since the dispute squarely falls within the ambit of Indian Telegraph Act, 1885 and respondent No.2- Tahasildar could not have entertained the application at the instance of respondent No.3.

For the reasons stated supra, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The writ petition is allowed in part.
ii) The letter issued by respondent No.2 is hereby set aside.
iii) Respondent No.3 if intends to lay electrical lines over the lands owned by the petitioner, they are bound to pay damages in terms of Section 10-D of the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885.
iv) In the event petitioner feels aggrieved in regard to compensation determined by respondent No.3, it is always open for him to seek appropriate remedy under Section 16(4) of the Indian Telegraph Act.
v) Respondent No.3 is reserved with liberty to seek appropriate remedies under Section NC: 2023:KHC-D:10478 16(1) of the Act after paying compensation to the petitioner under Section 10-D of the Act.
vi) In view of disposal of the petition, pending interlocutory applications, if any, do not survive for consideration and are disposed of accordingly.
